ladder.question: What total amount of guarantees, credit-support commitments and minimum-revenue guarantees extended to AI labs and cloud partners will NVIDIA disclose as of the end of its fiscal 2027 (late January 2027), in its fiscal 2027 Form 10-K?

not_judged.part: versus the equity investments it has made
not_judged.why: NVIDIA's equity investments are a different quantity, so the comparison with them is not judged; the question tracks only the disclosed total of guarantees and credit support.

not_judged.part: the credit support for nearly 2 gigawatts of computing capacity for one additional AI lab, not yet signed and checked within 18 months
not_judged.why: Whether that credit support is signed is a separate event with its own check date; the question counts it in the total only as far as the annual report discloses it.

figure.favourable_why: A smaller total leaves NVIDIA less exposed to losses if the AI labs and cloud partners it backs fail to pay, a risk the item asks investors to monitor.

ladder.question: What total of purchase obligations and supply and capacity commitments will NVIDIA report as of the end of its fiscal 2027 (late January 2027), in the contractual obligations and purchase commitment disclosures of its fiscal 2027 Form 10-K?

not_judged.why: The change from the prior year's amount is a comparison; the question judges the fiscal 2027 amount itself.

figure.favourable_why: Smaller purchase commitments leave NVIDIA less exposed to inventory write-downs and fixed cash outflows if AI demand slows.

ladder.question: Will the U.S. government authorise the export of any of NVIDIA's current Blackwell-generation data-center AI chips to customers in China by 2027-01-31, the end of NVIDIA's fiscal 2027?

not_judged.part: whether Chinese authorities stop restricting Nvidia chip shipments (Chinese acceptance of shipments)
not_judged.why: It is a separate decision by a different government, on which an analyst would hold its own view; the question judges only the U.S. export approval.

not_judged.part: so that China data-center revenue can resume
not_judged.why: NVIDIA's China revenue is the company's own figure that would follow from both approvals; the question judges the U.S. decision.
An approval limited to approved customers still counts as the approval; the scope of customers is a difference inside the outcome.

event.happened: By 2027-01-31 the U.S. government has authorised the export of at least one of NVIDIA's Blackwell-generation data-center AI chips to customers in China, through an export licence granted to NVIDIA, a published Commerce Department rule or an announced approval.

ruled_out.by_whom: The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security
ruled_out.decision: The U.S. Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security formally denies NVIDIA's request to export Blackwell-generation chips to China, or issues a rule that bars their export to China, after 2026-09-23.

ladder.question: Will NVIDIA begin volume customer shipments of its Vera Rubin platform, with first revenue from them recognised, within its fiscal 2027 (by 2027-01-31), as shown in its quarterly results or fiscal 2027 Form 10-K?

event.happened: NVIDIA's quarterly results or fiscal 2027 Form 10-K report that NVIDIA shipped Vera Rubin platform products to customers and recognised revenue from them within fiscal 2027, that is by 2027-01-31.

ruled_out.decision: NVIDIA announces after 2026-09-23 that it has cancelled the Vera Rubin platform or that its first customer shipments are postponed beyond 2027-01-31.

ladder.question: How much will the big five AI hyperscalers spend in total on data-center capital expenditure in calendar 2026, as reported in their full-year 2026 earnings releases and Form 10-K filings?

reference.words: the big five AI hyperscalers will spend nearly $800 billion on data centers this year

ladder.question: Will NVIDIA complete its agreed acquisition of Hugging Face for approximately $12.9 billion by 2028-03-24, as shown in NVIDIA's press releases, Form 8-K or periodic filings?

not_judged.why: A completion at a price other than about $12.9 billion still counts as completion; the price is a difference inside the outcome, not what the question judges.

event.happened: NVIDIA has completed (closed) its acquisition of Hugging Face by 2028-03-24, as announced in an NVIDIA press release, Form 8-K or periodic filing.

ruled_out.by_whom: NVIDIA, Hugging Face, or a competition authority or court
ruled_out.decision: NVIDIA or Hugging Face terminates the acquisition agreement, or a competition authority or court blocks the acquisition, after 2026-09-25.

reference.words: The company also recently agreed to acquire Hugging Face for approximately $12.9 billion to expand its software capabilities.

ladder.question: Will China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology approve purchases of NVIDIA's RTX Pro 5500 GPU by Alibaba, ByteDance or other Chinese companies by 2027-01-31, the end of NVIDIA's fiscal 2027?

not_judged.part: so that Nvidia can ship the product into China and book related revenue
not_judged.why: NVIDIA's shipments and revenue in China are the company's own figures that follow from the approval; the question judges only the ministry's decision.
An approval that limits the number of chips still counts as an approval; the approved quantity is a difference inside the outcome.

not_judged.part: approval for each of Alibaba, ByteDance and the other Chinese firms
not_judged.why: An approval of purchases by any of these companies counts; which companies are approved is a difference inside the outcome.

event.happened: By 2027-01-31 China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has approved purchases of NVIDIA's RTX Pro 5500 by Alibaba, ByteDance or another Chinese company, as shown by an official Chinese government announcement, a disclosure by NVIDIA or the buyer, or reports of the approval in major news outlets.

ruled_out.by_whom: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
ruled_out.decision: China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, or another Chinese government authority, formally refuses or bans Chinese companies' purchases of NVIDIA's RTX Pro 5500 after 2026-09-27.

reference.words: the ministry told some of the firms it intends to approve the purchases

answer.no_ladder: The question tracks global venture funding raised by physical AI (robotics) startups in calendar 2026, a matter that none of the listed themes covers (AI capital spending tracks spending on AI infrastructure, not startups' venture fundraising), and it is not NVIDIA's own figure.

ladder.question: How much will the big five AI hyperscalers spend in total on data-center capital expenditure in calendar 2027, as reported in their full-year 2027 earnings releases and Form 10-K filings?

not_judged.part: the nearly $800 billion expected for calendar 2026
not_judged.why: That is calendar 2026 spending, a different year's figure; the question judges calendar 2027 spending against the $1.3 trillion projection.

reference.words: the current estimates are for their capex to rise to $1.3 trillion next year

ladder.question: How many gigawatts of new data-center capacity will be added in the United States in calendar 2026, as measured by full-year 2026 industry data-center capacity reports (such as CBRE's and JLL's North America data center reports) and grid-operator data?

not_judged.part: against how far labour availability constrains that pace
not_judged.why: The labour constraint is a cause of the pace, not the capacity figure the question judges.

reference.words: the US is adding "somewhere between 10, 20 gigawatts a year" of the infrastructure

ladder.question: By how much, in percent, will the average DRAM contract price (including HBM) in calendar 2026 change from its calendar 2025 average, according to TrendForce/DRAMeXchange's full-year 2026 contract price data?

not_judged.part: as Nvidia reports substantially higher memory and component costs across the industry
not_judged.why: NVIDIA's own component costs are a different figure; the question judges only the industry's DRAM contract prices.

ladder.question: Will NVIDIA sign and disclose a binding guarantee of hardware residual values for the AI infrastructure financing platform it is building with financial partners, as it proposed (sharing up to $125 billion in risk), by 2028-04-03, as shown in its press releases or SEC filings?

not_judged.part: and at what amount, versus being reduced from the up-to-$125 billion proposed
not_judged.why: The size of the signed guarantee is a second figure; the question judges only whether a guarantee is signed and disclosed, whatever its amount.

event.happened: By 2028-04-03 NVIDIA has signed a definitive agreement to guarantee hardware residual values for its AI infrastructure financing platform and disclosed it in a press release or an SEC filing (Form 8-K, 10-Q or 10-K).

ruled_out.by_whom: NVIDIA or its financial partners in the platform
ruled_out.decision: NVIDIA formally withdraws its proposal to guarantee hardware residual values, or NVIDIA and its financial partners abandon the AI infrastructure financing platform, after 2026-10-03.

reference.words: Nvidia also proposed sharing up to $125 billion in risk by guaranteeing hardware residual values.

ladder.question: How many co-packaged-optics (CPO) switches will NVIDIA ship in its fiscal 2028 (February 2027 to January 2028), as stated in NVIDIA's quarterly results, management commentary or fiscal 2028 Form 10-K?

not_judged.part: the Q4 2026, early-2027 and mid-2027 checkpoints (15,000, 16,000 and 30,000 units)
not_judged.why: Shipments for a quarter or part of a year are evidence toward the full-year figure, not judged questions of their own.

figure.favourable_why: More CPO switches shipped means more networking revenue from a newer, higher-value product line.

reference.words: For all of 2027, shipments could reach 100,000 units.
